$comment: Hand-maintained reference of the [ClashEngine] INI configuration knobs operators set in SubspaceServer's global.conf / arena.conf. This is documentation, NOT a consumed schema: the source of truth is the parsers under src/ClashEngine/Config/ (and ClashModule.cs for the plug-in-tuning keys). When you add or change a knob there, update the matching entry here and the table in README.md. Each knob lists the exact code site it is read from so the three can be diffed.

scopeLegend.zone: Read from global.conf only (_config.Global). Zone-wide. Only the plug-in-tuning keys live here.
scopeLegend.arena: Read from the arena's arena.conf (plus #includes). Per-arena. Game types and queues are arena-scoped only; a GameType/Queue block in global.conf is ignored (ClashEngine warns if it finds one).

typeLegend.duration: Bare integer = seconds, or HH:MM:SS. Parsed by ConfigReadHelpers.TryReadTimeSpan.
typeLegend.enum: One of the listed literals, case-insensitive.
typeLegend.indexedBlock: Repeated <i> from 1..Count, where Count is the companion '*Count' key.

groups.title: Plug-in tuning
groups.note: Read once at module load from global.conf. LogVerbosity is also runtime-mutable via ?clashlog.

knobs.description: Log detail level. Verbose adds command/event/orchestrator debug; Trace adds every wire event. Runtime-mutable via ?clashlog.

Stats-upload endpoint receiving the multipart/form-data match POST (metadata JSON + replay). Both UploadUrl and UploadApiKey must be set, or ClashEngine writes match envelopes as JSON files under <BaseDirectory>/matches instead.
Sent as the X-Api-Key header on the upload POST. Required (with UploadUrl) for HTTP upload.
Per-match viewer URL broadcast after the scoreboard. May contain a literal {matchId} token (replaced with the dashed GUID); without one the id is appended. Unset suppresses the line.
Record every started match with the in-plug-in MatchRecorder.
Where in-flight .replay files land. Files are deleted after a successful upload.
Sampling frequency of the distance-to-nearest-enemy sampler feeding the scoreboard's dE column. 0 disables.

groups.title: Game types
groups.note: GameTypeCount = N -> reads GameType1..GameTypeN from arena.conf. A game type is the rules of one match shape; many queues can reference one game type by name. Arena-scoped only: a GameType block in global.conf is ignored (ClashEngine warns if GameTypeCount/QueueCount appear there). Game-type NAMES form a single zone-wide namespace and are globally referenceable: declare a name once in any arena.conf and any arena's Queue<i>GameType can reference it (resolution is attach-order-independent). Declare each name once -- a second arena declaring the same name is rejected (first definer wins); do NOT #include the same GameType block into multiple arenas (that collides). Game types are sticky: once registered they persist for the process lifetime even after the declaring arena detaches. A duplicate name within one arena (case-insensitive) is skipped with a Warn. A slot that fails a required-field or constraint check is skipped entirely.

knobs.description: Registry identifier referenced by Queue<j>GameType. Case-insensitive. Missing -> the slot is skipped.
Display string used in chat output and the stats-server registration POST.
Optional long-form description carried on the stats-server registration POST.
Number of teams. Below 2 -> the game type is skipped.
Players per team. Below 1 -> the game type is skipped.
Per-team kills required to win. 0 = unset. If neither KillTarget nor TimeLimit is set, the end policy falls back to first-to-30 kills. Negative -> coerced to 0.
Leader at this elapsed time wins; a tie triggers sudden-death overtime. May coexist with KillTarget (whichever fires first ends the match). <= 0 -> ignored.
Elimination matches: total lives per player counting the initial spawn (0 = unlimited). Negative -> coerced to 0.
Master switch for deterministic spawn warping. Off -> all Team<t>Spawns / MaxSpawnDrift coordinates are silently ignored and arena defaults apply.
Per-team candidate spawn coordinates in pixels for t in 1..TeamCount. The orchestrator picks one entry uniformly at random per match and warps the whole team there. Gated by WarpOnSpawn.
Max drift from the chosen spawn during Staging/Countdown before a player is warped back. null or 0 disables drift enforcement. Negative -> ignored.

Upper bound on the warmup window between formation and countdown. Ends early once every participant flips non-idle; a still-idle player at the limit cancels the match. <= 0 -> dropped to engine default.
Length of the pre-GO countdown. Ships lock 5s before GO. <= 0 -> dropped to engine default.
Grace between a player's last-life death and the forced spec, so residual mines/bombs can land. Only meaningful for elimination matches (Lives > 0). Negative -> dropped to default.
How long a whole team can have no Active or Pending players before forfeiting. Negative -> dropped to default.

After a non-fatal death, the window in which a player may change ships before being re-locked to their current ship for the rest of the life. 0 forbids every in-match ship change. Negative -> dropped to default.

Inventory policy on ?return after self-spec. full keeps the fresh loadout; restore deducts back to what the player had at spec (closes the burst/repel reload loophole); burn zeros the loadout. Unrecognized -> Full.

groups.title: Queues
groups.note: QueueCount = N -> reads Queue1..QueueN from arena.conf. Each queue is one matchmaking pool producing matches under a referenced game type. A queue whose GameType is missing/unknown (not in the accepted set) is dropped with a Warn. Many policy knobs have two defaults: a standard one and a more lenient one applied by Preset=casual; an explicit Queue<i><Key> always overrides the preset.

knobs.description: Lookup identifier. Players type it with ?play <name>; multiple space-separated tokens join with '_' (so ?play casual 4v4 -> casual_4v4). Case-insensitive. Missing -> the slot is skipped.
Must match a GameType<j>Name in the accepted set. Many queues can share one game type. Missing or unknown -> the queue is skipped.
Pretty display string for chat output and the JSON match-stats payload. Decouples display from the lookup name.

Opt-in lenient bundle: qStart/qFloor 0.4/0.10 (vs 0.6/0.30), no MaxLiabilityGap cap, RelaxTime 45s, RatingWeight 0.5, griefing teamkill threshold 3 (vs 2). Each knob is still individually overridable. Unrecognized -> ignored (standard defaults apply).
Arena players are sent to for the match. Recommended: a dedicated arena listed in PermanentArenas.
Extra candidates above the minimum (TotalPlayers) the matcher considers for the best partition. 0 = strict FIFO. Negative -> coerced to 0. The engine's pool size is TotalPlayers + this.
How fast the quality threshold decays from qStart to qFloor. Longer = stricter early; shorter = accepts weaker matches sooner. <= 0 -> dropped to default.
Once a viable partition is found, how long the matcher waits for a better one. 0 pops immediately. Negative -> dropped to default.
If a held candidate's quality reaches this, pop without waiting out the hold window. Out of range -> dropped to default.
Distinct match participants who must ?forgive a pending griefing penalty within VetoWindow to rescind it. Below 1 -> dropped to default.
Open period for vetos after a griefing flag fires; the penalty becomes final at the end if the threshold wasn't reached. <= 0 -> dropped to default.
KOTH mode: the winning team auto-re-enqueues at the head of this queue after a Completed match.
Max consecutive wins a champion can defend before going to the back of the queue. Only meaningful with PromoteWinners=1. Below 1 -> dropped to default.
Base queue name ?play resolves to when issued from this arena without an explicit queue. Read from arena scope only. Unset -> ?play requires a named queue.

derivedKnobs.$comment: Settings an operator does NOT set directly via a conf key, but which are derived from the knobs above and surface in behavior / the stats payload. Listed so the registry documents the full effective surface.

items.name: RatingWeight
items.description: Match importance toward rating updates. No standalone conf key.

items.name: MatchShape.MaxLiabilityGap
items.description: Cap on the rating gap of the weakest player. No standalone conf key.

items.name: GriefingHeuristic
items.value: Lives>0 -> EarlyExitHeuristic (2-min min duration); else TeamkillThresholdHeuristic (threshold 3 casual / 2 standard)
items.description: Griefing detector selected from the game type and preset. No standalone conf key.

items.name: GameTypeMetadata
items.description: Auto-derived stats-server metadata blob (teamCount/teamSizes/livesPerPlayer). There is intentionally no GameType<i>Metadata conf key.
